summary: Strong audio/input engineering undermined by a confirmed, reproducible CSS layout bug that clips a required section entirely off-screen. Verified in a real browser (Playwright, served artifact/dist) at both graded viewports: at 1440x900, .control-deck-surface (src/styles.css:166-171) lays out six flex children with `flex: 0 0 X%` and no min-width override; the Piano section's content cannot fit its 8.5% allocation (renders at 264.6px / 21.4% instead of ~105px) and, because flex-shrink is 0 combined with default min-width:auto, the row's total content (~1642px including 4px gaps) exceeds the 1239px deck width. .chassis-main-body's `overflow: hidden` (styles.css:116) then silently clips the trailing ~403px: the entire Layer Effects section (#section-effects, 6 effect units + layer-focus buttons) is 100% invisible (getBoundingClientRect x:1459-1742, entirely past the visible right edge at x:1345.7), and roughly the right third of the Synth section (filter Freq/Res/Drive/KB-Env, Amp Envelope, Mod Env, LFO & Arp) is also cut off, confirmed by cropping the desktop screenshot at the 'FILTER / TYPE' label where the chassis end-cheek appears immediately after. This reproduces exactly in the candidate's own sealed evidence (artifact/evidence/stage1-desktop.png and stage1-narrow.png show only 5 of 6 sections) and persists at 390x844 even after scrolling the horizontally-scrollable stage fully right (mainBody clips internally, independent of page scroll). This directly violates the phase-1 hard gate 'The complete visible control surface is present with the documented section geometry' and the regression.chassis hard gate ('no ... clipped chassis at 1440x900 and 390x844'). Critically, the candidate's own regression.chassis and visual.section-layout tests (src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx:45-84,148-157) only assert DOM node presence and the inline `style.flex` string, never real computed layout/bounding boxes, so this screenshot-visible defect passed every automated gate undetected. Apart from this structural failure, the implemented surfaces are high quality: the basic piano voice (additive synthesis, src/audio/PianoVoice.ts) has real velocity-to-brightness/gain mapping, register-dependent decay/release, deterministic voice stealing (src/audio/PianoEngine.ts:172-190), and full cleanup on blur/visibilitychange/unmount (src/App.tsx:57-83); pointer/touch/keyboard/MIDI all funnel through one injectable NoteLifecycle with correct multi-source note ownership (src/input/NoteLifecycle.ts:27-61) and a fully injectable, testable MidiController (src/input/MidiController.ts). Decorative controls are verified honest: grepping the codebase confirms no panel state (master_level, hardwareState, etc.) is ever read by PianoEngine/PianoVoice, and IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json truthfully declares the voice as generated additive synthesis, not a recording.

criteria.label: Silhouette, chassis, and geometry
evidence: Overall chassis silhouette is strong: continuous red chassis (nord-stage-4-chassis, styles.css:85-92), correct 54/46 deck/keybed vertical split (chassis-deck-zone height calc(54% - 12px), styles.css:137-142; chassis-keybed-zone height 46%, styles.css:151-157), wooden end cheeks, and exact 73-key E1-E7 keybed (73 keys, 43 white/30 black, verified in src/model/keyboard.ts and src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx:8-28) matching specs/nord-stage-4.variants.json.

However, the section-width geometry the same criterion explicitly covers ('section widths') is broken in the real render: SECTION_WIDTH_FRACTIONS in src/model/hardware.ts:277-284 correctly encodes performance 0.14/organ 0.20/piano 0.085/program 0.125/synth 0.25/effects 0.20, and ControlDeck.tsx:22-44 applies these as inline flex-basis percentages, but Playwright measurement of the live artifact/dist build at 1440x900 shows the Piano section wrapper actually renders at 264.56px (21.35% of the 1239.44px deck) instead of ~105px (8.5%), because its content (two level faders + 6-type list + 6 detail buttons in a ~105px column) cannot fit and flex-shrink is 0 with default min-width:auto (no override in styles.css).

This single overflow cascades: measured wrapper widths sum to ~1621.6px + 5x4px gaps = ~1641.6px against a 1239.44px container -> ~402px overflow, which .chassis-main-body's `overflow: hidden` (styles.css:116) clips from the right edge, deleting the entire Effects section from view and around a third of the Synth section (see hardwareInventory evidence). The rendered silhouette is therefore visually incomplete/incorrect at the section level despite the correct outer chassis shape.

criteria.label: Complete hardware inventory and placement
evidence: Confirmed via Playwright on the served artifact/dist build (http://127.0.0.1:8936, viewport 1440x900) and reproduced in the sealed evidence images (artifact/evidence/stage1-desktop.png, stage1-narrow.png): only 5 of the 6 required sections (performance, organ, piano, program, synth) are visible; the Layer Effects section is completely absent from the rendered surface.

DOM/computed-style measurement: #section-effects getBoundingClientRect = {x:1459.3, width:282.5} while .chassis-main-body (the clipping ancestor, overflow:hidden) right edge is at x:94.28+1251.44=1345.7 -> the entire Effects section (Effect 1, Effect 2, Delay, Amp/EQ, Compressor, Reverb, and the 3 layer-focus buttons, all coded correctly in src/components/sections/EffectsSection.tsx) renders 100% outside the visible/clipped area, at every viewport tested (also reproduced at 390x844 even after scrolling the .instrument-stage container fully right - the clip is internal to the chassis and independent of page scroll).

A visual crop of the desktop screenshot at the right edge (Synth section) shows the panel is truncated immediately after the 'FILTER / TYPE' label, i.e. Filter Freq/Res/Drive/KB-Env knobs, the full Amp Envelope (ATT/DEC/SUS/REL), Mod Envelope, and LFO & Arp block -- all present in the DOM per src/components/sections/SynthSection.tsx and the accessibility snapshot -- are also visually cut off, matching the measured Synth wrapper rect (x:1105-1449.4) exceeding the mainBody right edge (x:1345.7) by ~104px.

Program and Synth remain the only primary OLED locations in the DOM (src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx:130-145 asserts exactly 2 .oled-display-screen nodes, in #section-program and #section-synth only) -- this part of the requirement is correctly implemented in markup, but is moot for a large chunk of the Synth section's content given the clipping.

This is a direct violation of hard gate 2 ('The complete visible control surface is present with the documented section geometry, and Program and Synth are the only primary OLED locations') since roughly 1/3 of the deck's control surface (all of Effects, part of Synth) is not visible to a sighted user despite being correctly authored in source.

criteria.label: Materials, color, typography, and displays
evidence: Chassis reds (#851a25 mid / #5a0c13 dark, matching specs/nord-stage-4.visual.json referenceColors) and panel blue-gray (#3c424d) are used correctly per artifact/src/styles.css custom properties and are visually convincing in artifact/evidence/stage1-desktop.png against reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg.

OLED displays (src/components/controls/OledDisplay.tsx) render cyan/green monospace-styled text on a dark bezel with a glow, matching the reference photo's OLED aesthetic; LED ladders on drawbars (src/components/controls/Drawbar.tsx:93-104) light progressively red as value increases.
Typography, branding ('nord stage 4' logo, HA73 sub-label), and section title bars are legible and consistent with Nord's condensed sans branding seen in the reference photo.

Minor deviations from photographic fidelity (flatter gradients/shadows than the product photo, drawbar cap colors slightly simplified) keep this from a top score, but nothing here is broken or dishonest -- the visible parts of the deck (Performance, Organ, Piano, Program, and the visible fraction of Synth) are materially faithful.

criteria.label: Narrow retention
evidence: At 390x844 (artifact/evidence/stage1-narrow.png and live Playwright verification), the same clipping bug from hardwareInventory persists: #section-effects remains fully outside .chassis-main-body's clipped bounds even after setting stage.scrollLeft = 99999 (mainBodyWidth measured 922px at narrow, effects rect still x:741.9-1024.4 relative to the clip boundary at x:922) -- i.e. there is no scroll position at which Layer Effects or the tail of Synth become visible, directly violating 'no clipping or lost controls' for the narrow viewport.

Positive: no vertical scroll issue, no marketing hero, chassis and keybed remain legibly inspectable via the horizontal pan that IS available (min-width:980px media query at styles.css:77-81), and the status bar / AUDIO/MIDI/VOICES/SUSTAIN indicators remain visible and legible at the bottom of the narrow layout.

Because the missing/clipped content is identical to the desktop case and represents real, permanently-lost controls (not just requiring more scrolling), this scores low rather than a mid-range partial-credit rating.

criteria.label: Unified playable inputs
evidence: Single shared note lifecycle: src/input/NoteLifecycle.ts:27-61 tracks per-MIDI-note 'sources' (pointer/touch/keyboard/midi) in a Map<number, Set<NoteSource>> and only calls engine.noteOff when the last source releases, correctly modeling independent multi-touch and multi-source overlap; verified by src/__tests__/audio.test.ts:38-71 (pointer holds, keyboard also holds, pointer releases -> note stays on, keyboard releases -> note off).

Pointer/touch unified via Pointer Events with setPointerCapture/releasePointerCapture and pointercancel handling (src/components/Keybed.tsx:17-77), enabling glissando via handlePointerEnter (lines 34-40) and safe cleanup on drag-off-window via pointercancel.

Computer keyboard mapped via COMPUTER_KEY_MAP with OS auto-repeat suppression (NoteLifecycle.ts:80-102, e.repeat check) and Space-bar-as-sustain with textarea/input guard; verified live (dispatched raw keydown/keyup events; VOICES count and SUSTAIN pill correctly reflected state changes) and in src/__tests__/interaction.test.tsx:30-58.

MIDI implemented against an injectable GenericMidiAccess interface (src/input/MidiController.ts) rather than the raw browser API, enabling deterministic tests for granted/denied/disconnected states and CC64 sustain and Note On/Off parsing (src/__tests__/audio.test.ts:73-139); denied/disconnected MIDI correctly reported to the UI (live snapshot showed 'MIDI: PENDING' -> after mock access, would show granted/denied deterministically per tests).
Window blur and document visibilitychange both trigger lifecycle.allNotesOff() (src/App.tsx:57-65), and this is exercised live and in interaction.test.tsx:54-57 (blur test).

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle and performance
evidence: Velocity affects both gain and brightness: PianoVoice.ts:48-57 scales lowpass cutoff (`baseFreq * (2.5 + velocity*8.0)`) and peak gain (`velocity^1.4 * 0.28`) with note velocity; proven by src/__tests__/audio.test.ts:142-168 which asserts a hard-velocity note produces a strictly higher filter cutoff than a soft one via the real Web Audio node graph (mocked context, but real parameter scheduling code path).

Register-dependent release/decay: PianoVoice.ts:55 (`decayTime = max(1.5, 9.0 - (midi-28)*0.09)`) and :127 (`releaseDuration = max(0.12, 0.35 - (midi-28)*0.003)`) implement acoustically plausible longer sustain/release for bass notes.

Polyphony with deterministic voice stealing: PianoEngine.ts:172-190 prioritizes stealing a releasing voice, then a sustained voice, then the oldest active voice, verified by src/__tests__/audio.test.ts:170-190 (9 notes into an 8-voice-max engine, count stays capped at 8).

Overlap/repeat verified live: dispatched pointerdown on key-60 then key-64 while both held raised VOICES from 1 to 2 (concurrent voices, confirmed via the app's own voice-count telemetry reading engine.getActiveVoiceCount()).

Sustain correctly gates per-note release (PianoEngine.ts:138-166, noteOff defers to 'sustained' state while isSustainActive, and setSustain(false) releases only voices that were held solely by sustain) and was exercised live: holding Space showed 'SUSTAIN: HOLD (ON)' while VOICES remained non-zero.

Full cleanup with node disconnect on stop (PianoVoice.ts:164-199 disconnects all oscillators, gains, filter) tied to blur/visibilitychange/unmount in App.tsx:57-83, and engine.dispose() closes the AudioContext (PianoEngine.ts:215-237).

criteria.label: Basic source and status honesty
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json truthfully labels the voice as 'Web Audio API real-time acoustic piano additive & physical harmonic synthesis' under generatedSources (not sampleSources), matching the honesty contract; verification.json corroborates generatedSources:1, sampleSources:0.

AudioStatus lifecycle (uninitialized/loading/ready/error/suspended, src/audio/types.ts:1) is wired end-to-end: StatusBar.tsx shows the live status pill and a 'Start Audio' action for uninitialized/suspended states (StatusBar.tsx:28-37), and engine.init() correctly transitions loading->ready or ->error (PianoEngine.ts:48-74); live testing confirmed clicking 'Start Audio' worked and subsequent note-ons produced voices.

Gap: the 'error' AudioStatus has no retry affordance or distinct fallback messaging in StatusBar.tsx (the Start Audio button only renders for 'uninitialized'/'suspended', not 'error'), so a genuine AudioContext-construction failure would leave the user with a static, unrecoverable 'ERROR' label and no described fallback path, falling short of 'a labeled playable fallback' in the strictest reading of the piano spec's required scope.

criteria.label: Control movement and feedback
evidence: All controls that ARE visible move/press correctly with real feedback: live-tested Master Level knob (pointer-drag angle rotation + Arrow/Home/End keyboard per Knob.tsx:72-96), Organ drawbars (Home/End set 0/8 per Drawbar.tsx:62-86, LED ladder updates), buttons toggle aria-pressed (interaction.test.tsx:61-73), and keys press/release/cancel with visual key-pressed state and aria-pressed (Keybed.tsx, interaction.test.tsx:7-28).

However, per the hardwareInventory finding, the entire Layer Effects section (6 effect units, ~10+ interactive knobs/buttons) and roughly a third of the Synth section (Filter Freq/Res/Drive/KB-Env, Amp Envelope x4, Mod Envelope x3, LFO & Arp controls) are not visible on screen at either graded viewport, so a real user operating the instrument visually cannot see, let alone exercise, a significant fraction of the 'every visible input must move/press' surface -- these controls are only reachable via devtools/accessibility-tree inspection, not through the rendered UI a grader would interact with.
This materially reduces the practically exercisable control surface even though the underlying component code (EffectsSection.tsx, SynthSection.tsx) is fully interactive and well-implemented.

criteria.label: Decorative-control boundary
evidence: Source-level audit: grepping the codebase for `master_level`/`hardwareState` shows PianoEngine.ts and PianoVoice.ts never reference HardwareState or any panel-control value -- the audio graph is driven purely by NoteLifecycle-supplied (midi, velocity, sustain) parameters, confirming panel controls cannot alter the audio graph.

IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json note explicitly states 'All panel controls move and update presentation state accessibly without altering the audio signal, honoring the honesty contract,' and src/__tests__/interaction.test.tsx:61-73 verifies decorative buttons toggle only aria-pressed/local state.

The Effects section's on/bypass/type/rate/amount controls (EffectsSection.tsx) are coded with exactly this decorative pattern (updateState only, no engine/audio wiring) and would be honest if visible; they cannot be independently confirmed by a sighted grader through normal interaction because of the clipping defect described under hardwareInventory/physicalInteraction, which is why this does not score a 4 despite the code being correct.

criteria.label: Data structure and tests
evidence: Well-normalized, stable-ID hardware model: src/model/hardware.ts defines a single flat, typed HardwareState (lines 13-143) with a SECTION_WIDTH_FRACTIONS source of truth (lines 277-284) matching the spec, and clean input/audio/model/component separation (src/input, src/audio, src/model, src/components).

Meaningful, non-trivial tests exist for audio behavior via a hand-rolled MockAudioContext/Node/Param (src/__tests__/audio-mock.ts) that records real scheduled parameter values, letting audio.test.ts:142-168 assert an actual numeric relationship (harder velocity -> higher filter cutoff) rather than a boolean flag; this is better than a pure state-only fake but still short of the task's stated audio-test bar of proving output differs from silence via real rendered signal analysis (e.g. OfflineAudioContext + analyser), since nothing here renders or measures actual samples.

Critical gap: the regression.chassis and visual.section-layout tests (src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx:45-84, 148-157) that are supposed to guard exactly the defect found in this evaluation only check `document.querySelector(...)` presence and the literal `style.flex` inline-style string (e.g. `expect(fxWrapper.style.flex).toContain('20%')`), never actual computed layout, getBoundingClientRect, or overflow -- jsdom does not perform real flex layout, so this test suite is structurally incapable of catching the confirmed clipped-chassis / missing-section defect described above, despite the feature-matrix.json claiming coverage for 'regression.chassis'. This is a meaningful test-quality and false-confidence issue in an area with a real, sealed-evidence-visible regression.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: verification.json confirms all four required technical checks (test, typecheck, lint, build) pass; live console inspection of the served artifact/dist build showed zero real errors (only benign favicon.ico 404s, unrelated to app logic).

Cleanup is robust: App.tsx:67-83 removes all window/document listeners and disposes MidiController/NoteLifecycle/PianoEngine on unmount; PianoVoice.cleanup() (PianoVoice.ts:164-199) disconnects every oscillator/gain/filter node.
Repeated interaction was stable in live testing (multiple note-on/off cycles, sustain hold/release, overlapping voices) with voice counts updating correctly and no console errors introduced.

However, 'runtime quality' also encompasses the actual rendered experience, and the confirmed clipped-chassis defect (hardwareInventory/responsiveRetention findings) is a real-browser rendering failure that none of the passing automated checks detect -- the technical gate (test/typecheck/lint/build) is green while the shipped, sealed evidence itself shows an incomplete instrument, which is the kind of gap 'runtime quality' assessment is meant to catch independent of the automated gate.

issues.description: The Layer Effects section (#section-effects in src/components/sections/EffectsSection.tsx) is completely invisible in the rendered instrument at both graded viewports (1440x900 and 390x844), and roughly the right third of the Synth section (Filter Freq/Res/Drive/KB-Env, Amp Envelope, Mod Envelope, LFO & Arp) is also clipped out of view. Root cause: ControlDeck.tsx:22-44 sets each section wrapper to `flex: '0 0 X%'` (flex-shrink:0) with no `min-width: 0` override in src/styles.css, so the Piano section's content (which needs far more than its 8.5% allocation) forces the wrapper to its content's min-content width (measured 264.6px vs the intended ~105px), overflowing the flex row by ~402px; `.chassis-main-body { overflow: hidden }` (styles.css:116) then silently clips that overflow from the trailing sections. Reproduced live via Playwright against the served artifact/dist build and confirmed identical in the candidate's own sealed evidence screenshots (artifact/evidence/stage1-desktop.png, stage1-narrow.png). This violates hard gate 2 ('complete visible control surface... documented section geometry') and the regression.chassis hard gate ('no... clipped chassis at 1440x900 and 390x844').

The candidate's own regression/visual test suite (src/__tests__/visual.test.tsx: 'visual.section-layout' and 'regression.chassis' describe blocks) cannot detect the above defect because it only asserts DOM node presence and the literal inline `style.flex` string rather than real computed layout or bounding-box overflow (jsdom does not perform genuine flex-box layout). The feature-matrix.json claims these feature IDs are covered, but the coverage is not meaningful for the specific structural regression that occurred.

StatusBar.tsx only renders a 'Start Audio' retry affordance for the 'uninitialized' and 'suspended' AudioStatus values, not for 'error' (StatusBar.tsx:28-37), so a genuine audio-initialization failure leaves the user with a static, non-actionable 'ERROR' label rather than a clearly labeled recovery/fallback path as implied by the piano spec's 'truthful loading/ready/error state and a labeled playable fallback' requirement.
